name: Elliot Reed
life: “I still remember letting a stranger hear my home phone ring.” On Sunday, near the downtown fountain, Elliot keeps a little time free to hear who is playing at the far end of the park.
voice: I sublet my sofa last winter and learned the difference between having room and having privacy.
appearance: Elliot has a wide brow and a narrow jaw. Look for a long silver braid. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is a charcoal zip cardigan with a replacement button a shade darker than the others. In conversation Elliot draws small circles on a tabletop while waiting.
personality: Elliot carries anger into a conversation very slowly. Once it arrives, a quiet statement of facts can be considerably harder to sidestep than a shout.
agenda: To agree how much privacy a new occupant needs.
family: Lara Emery is Elliot’s younger relative by marriage. Elliot gets to change the plan. Lara offers the first invitation. They learned that a promise to visit is easier to keep when changing a time does not count as letting down the whole family. Asked about *The sandwich board*, Lara says, “I carried the board home and it blocked my front door.”
connections: Aubrey Carver. The offered sofa has to work for two children and the person already sleeping there.

reactions.situation: A relative offers the family a sofa with conditions
reactions.response: Elliot asks what using the sofa would mean for the people already living there.

reactions.situation: A coworker arrives late after a night at the hospital
reactions.response: Elliot takes one immediate task off their hands and asks when they want to tell the supervisor.
reactions.asWritten: A coworker arrives late after a night at the hospital. Elliot takes one immediate task off their hands and asks when they want to tell the supervisor.

reactions.situation: If a friend asks for a false alibi for an ordinary missed appointment
reactions.response: Elliot offers to accompany them while they tell the truth.
